articles.summary: NBA News: Jaden Bradley just turned a training camp battle into a four-year paycheck. The Toronto Raptors converted the 23-year-old guard's two-way contract int.
articles.body: Jaden Bradley just turned a training camp battle into a four-year paycheck. The Toronto Raptors converted the 23-year-old guard's two-way contract into a standard deal worth $9.3 million on Monday, according to Michael Scotto of HoopsHype, with the first season fully guaranteed.Toronto's roster had dropped to 13 players once the long-negotiated Kawhi Leonard trade finally cleared, sending Brandon Ingram and Gradey Dick out west. Someone had to fill that open standard spot, and Bradley made the case himself.Jaden Bradley lands four-year Raptors dealJaden Bradley arrived in Toronto as the 50th pick of the 2026 draft, a slot usually reserved for camp fodder, not four-year commitments. He signed a two-way deal back on July 6 and spent the summer trying to make himself impossible to cut loose.He didn't dominate Summer League so much as show some unforgettable moments. Across five games, the Rochester, New York native averaged 6.4 points, 3.6 rebounds and 3.2 assists in just over 20 minutes a night, topping out at 15 points and five boards in a July 13 win over Indiana. Scotto's report on the new deal noted that "this first year of the deal is guaranteed," a detail that matters for a player who came in as one of the draft's final names.Bradley spent his final three college seasons at Arizona after starting his career at Alabama, where he made the All-SEC freshman team. By his senior year with the Wildcats, he was Big 12 Player of the Year, averaging 13.3 points, 4.4 assists, 3.4 rebounds and 1.4 steals while shooting 39.4 percent from three. He picked up Big 12 Tournament MVP and consensus Third Team All-American honors along the way and helped drag Arizona to its first Final Four in 25 years.Bradley now fights for backup point guard minutesNone of that guarantees playing time in Toronto. Bradley will spend training camp, which opens September 29 in Quebec City, competing for backup point guard reps behind Immanuel Quickley, with fellow Big 12 products Jamal Shead and Ja'Kobe Walter already in that mix. It's a crowded lane for a player who was a fringe draft name three months ago.Toronto didn't leave its two-way roster thin in the process. The team filled Bradley's old two-way slot with former Gonzaga guard Malachi Smith, keeping that development pipeline active even as Bradley graduates to the standard roster.For now, the deal looks like an investment rather than a promise for playing minutes. The Raptors are betting that the ball-handling, defense, and playmaking instincts that carried Arizona to a Final Four run translate better once an NBA season actually starts. articles.title: Angel Reese, Sabrina Ionescu's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights as Dream Beat Liberty
articles.summary: As the WNBA playoffs near and teams continue to fight for seeding, the Atlanta Dream picked up a crucial 95-84 win over the New York Liberty on Monday.
articles.body:
As the WNBA playoffs near and teams continue to fight for seeding, the Atlanta Dream picked up a crucial 95-84 win over the New York Liberty on Monday.

In their penultimate regular-season game, the Dream used strong performances from Jordin Canada and a double-double from Angel Reese to get past Sabrina Ionescu, Breanna Stewart and the Liberty.

As expected, it was a tight battle through, with the Dream holding just a three-point lead heading into halftime. Atlanta created some separation in the third quarter, though, thanks to a big run led by Rhyne Howard, Allisha Gray and DeWanna Bonner.

The Dream led by 11 heading into the final period and was able to keep things just out of reach down the stretch.

While both Atlanta and New York have already secured a spot in the playoffs, the game on Monday still has plenty of implications. The Dream are now closing on the third-placed Las Vegas Aces and will have the chance to jump them in the standings before the regular season ends.

The Liberty, meanwhile, fell two spots to the No. 8 seed with the loss, but they still can improve their standing before the playoffs.

Atlanta and New York will meet again on Wednesday in what should be an exciting clash to end the season.

The eight teams going to the WNBA playoffs have already been determined, but the fight is still on for postseason position as the league gets into its final week of play.

With the end of the regular season approaching on Thursday, here's a look at the current standings.

While the Minnesota Lynx are still in control of the top seed, it's far from a guarantee that they'll keep it through the end of the week. The Lynx will face Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever twice this week, and the Golden State Valkyries will be looking for them to slip up.

The Valkyries, meanwhile, have a relatively easy slate this week, taking on two non-playoff teams in the Portland Fire and Los Angeles Sparks. Golden State is looking to make a deep playoff run in its second-ever season, and securing the top seed would go a long way.

Like the Valkyries, the Atlanta Dream are hoping to jump up in the standings, and a win over the New York Liberty on Monday helps them get closer to third place while extending their lead on the No. 5 Fever.

The bottom four teams are all within a game or less of each other, so things could look much different by the end of the week.

Typically, the end of the season gives top teams the chance to relax a bit before the start of the playoffs, but that is far from the case this year. It certainly makes for an interesting final week of action ahead of what should be an exciting postseason.

articles.title: Breanna Stewart Calls On Angel Reese to Pay Fine After Rare Technical Foul in Liberty vs. Dream
articles.summary: For the first time in nearly a decade, Breanna Stewart earned a technical foul.
articles.body:
For the first time in nearly a decade, Breanna Stewart earned a technical foul.

The New York Liberty star was fired up at the officials after what she thought was a no-call on Angel Reese during Monday night's loss to the Atlanta Dream. Afterwards, she said Reese should pay the fine for the technical foul rather than her.

"That absolutely was [because of] the no-call," Stewart told reporters . "She slapped s--t out of my hand."

Despite being one of the league's biggest stars, Stewart typically holds her composure well even when calls aren't going her way. Monday marked the first time she has received a technical foul since 2017, and it's just the third of her career.

Clearly, it takes a lot to get a reaction out of Stewart, so she must have felt strongly that the refs missed the call on Reese.

The Liberty have already secured a playoff spot, but the loss to the Dream bumped them to the No. 8 seed . They'll look to improve their standing when they face Atlanta again on Wednesday.

articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon: Sydney policeman says he acted in self-defence in double murder trial
articles.summary: Beau Lamarre-Condon says his ex-partner and his new boyfriend were accidentally shot in separate struggles.
articles.body:
A Sydney policeman accused of killing his ex-partner and his new boyfriend while dressed as an Uber Eats rider says he was acting in self-defence, a court has heard.

Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, has pleaded not guilty to killing Jesse Baird, 26, and Baird's partner Luke Davies, 29, at a home in the suburb of Paddington in 2024.

In court on Tuesday, defence barrister John Stratton SC said the accused went to Baird's home to collect some belongings and wore a motorcycle helmet so as not to be recognised.

When he saw Baird after letting himself in, the pair struggled, ending when Baird was shot twice. Davies then picked up the gun and accidentally shot himself in a separate struggle, Stratton said.

During his opening address, Stratton said Lamarre-Condon did not murder the pair and that he had gone to the Baird's home that morning, expecting it would be empty.

Stratton said the reason the accused was dressed as an Uber Eats delivery driver was to avoid "the embarrassment of having a further meeting" with Baird, according to the Sydney Morning Herald.

Lamarre-Condon, who used a key given to him by Baird, was caught off guard when he saw Baird at home and the pair struggled as Baird did not recognise who it was due to the disguise, Stratton said.

After Baird was shot, the gun was "flung" across the room and Davies picked it up, Stratton told the court.

Lamarre-Condon then grabbed Davies' arm, pushing the gun away from himself and towards Davies, and during the tussle, Davies accidentally shot himself, the defence alleged.

The accused "understandably panicked" as "he knew this looked bad," Stratton said.

Earlier on Tuesday, the court heard audio of the alleged gunshots, with prosecutors saying Davies was shot as he tried to call Triple Zero.

Prosecutors also told the court that Lamarre-Condon had confessed to a friend that he had killed two people with a gun, and allegedly made a hand gesture and said "pew pew".

On the first day of the trial on Monday, the court heard how Lamarre-Condon and Baird, a TV presenter, had briefly dated before they split in late-2023.

Prosecutors, in their opening address on Monday, said the accused had developed an "obsessive and jealous infatuation" with Baird and that he had previously stolen a key to Baird's home.

In the weeks after they broke up, Lamarre-Condon used a friend's phone to message Baird and claim he had cancer, stalked his ex-lover, and tampered with his car, the prosecution alleged.

The jury trial is expected to last for up to 12 weeks.

articles.title: Batum se retira con una gran mancha en su carrera... su puñetazo a Navarro: "En España no me quieren"
articles.summary: Nicolas Batum, campeón del Eurobasket con Francia en 2013 que jugó 18 temporadas en la NBA, ha anunciado su retirada del baloncesto con 37 años.
articles.body: Nicolas Batum, campeón del Eurobasket con Francia en 2013 que jugó 18 temporadas en la NBA, ha anunciado su retirada del baloncesto con 37 años. "No me asusta dejar de ser jugador de baloncesto porque he vivido todo lo que tenía que vivir. He hecho todo lo que tenía que hacer. Quizá por eso me siento tan orgulloso. Hoy soy feliz", dijo Batum en el vídeo en el que comunicaba su retirada y compartía dos fechas: 21/09/1991 y 21/09/2026. En España no se olvida el 08/08/2012... el día que le pegó un puñetazo en el vientre a Juan Carlos Navarro en los Juegos Olímpicos de Londres. "¿En qué equipo de Europa jugaría? Sé que en Barcelona no sería bien recibido, por lo que pasó con su actual director deportivo (Juan Carlos Navarro). Eso quedó arreglado con él, pero no con los aficionados. No me quieren mucho en España... así que creo que jugar en España no sería bueno para mí", se sinceró Batum en 2024. En 2012 Batum ya declaró que "sé que no hice bien. Mi reacción estuvo muy mal y ya he pedido perdón", aunque en la misma rueda prensa sorprendió diciendo que "mucha gente a través de las redes sociales o de los medios me ha felicitado y me ha dado las gracias por esta acción. Incluso entrenadores y jugadores de otros equipos... Sólo querían felicitarme y créeme cuando te digo que ha sido mucha gente y no especialmente de Francia, sino de todo el mundo. No creo que sea algo por lo que felicitar a nadie. No estoy ni feliz ni orgulloso de ello".

articles.title: Dream news: Rhyne Howard reaches historic 3-pointers milestone in win vs. Liberty
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream are still jockeying for playoff positioning with the Las Vegas Aces, as they can still finish with the three-seed with the 2026 WNBA regula...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream are still jockeying for playoff positioning with the Las Vegas Aces , as they can still finish with the three-seed with the 2026 WNBA regular season winding down. On Monday, the Dream secured a 95-84 victory over the New York Liberty to improve to 29-14 on the season. If the Aces lose out to end the campaign and Atlanta wins its final game (also against the Liberty), they can finish above the reigning champion in the standings.

This season has merely been a continuation of the Dream's electric 2025 campaign, when they finished with a 30-14 record — blossoming into one of the best teams in the WNBA after finishing below .500 for six consecutive seasons prior.

One of the main driving forces for the Dream has been Rhyne Howard , the first overall pick of the 2022 WNBA Draft. She is the team's second-leading scorer (behind Allisha Gray ), and it's her p roficiency from beyond the arc that opens up a lot of space for Atlanta's offense. And while she did go just 2-8 from beyond the arc in their win over the Liberty on Monday, she still made history with her three-point production.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

By making two three-pointers, she now has 500 made threes for her career. The Dream guard then became the youngest player in WNBA history, at 26 years old and 146 days, and the fastest (178 career games) to reach that mark, as per the official WNBA account on X.

Howard has never been shy to let it fly from beyond the arc. For her career, she's averaging nearly nine attempts from deep per game (8.8), and she's made nearly three of them (2.8) per contest. She commands a ton of respect just due to her sheer willingness to let it fly, and in 2026, her efficiency from beyond the arc has reached a new level, as she's made over three triples per contest on a 36.0% clip — a career-best.

The Dream will need more of this sort of production from deep from Howard as they look to contend for the WNBA championship — something the franchise has never won in its 19-year history.

The Phoenix Mercury hosted the Dallas Wings at Mortgage Matchup Center on Monday, with NBA legend Chris Paul showing up to show support for the WNBA.

Paul pulled up at courtside, having a lively chat, most probably about basketball, with ex-WNBA forward Tamera Young.

The 41-year-old Paul has close ties with Phoenix, having starred for the Phoenix Suns from 2020 to 2023. In his first season with the Suns, he helped them reach the NBA Finals in 2021.

The future Hall of Famer, who retired in February, has always been a proud ally of the WNBA. In 2022, the league named him the inaugural recipient of the Kobe & Gigi Bryant Advocacy Award for his significant contributions to advancing girls' and women's basketball.

articles.title: Esta Liga no se arruga: 71 jugadores de más de 30 años en la ACB
articles.standfirst: La experiencia cotiza al alza en una Liga Endesa que se niega a mirar el DNI. Treintañeros y hasta cuarentones siguen sentando cátedra. Nico Laprovittola, el último gran protagonista
articles.summary: La experiencia cotiza al alza en una Liga Endesa que se niega a mirar el DNI. Treintañeros y hasta cuarentones siguen sentando cátedra. Nico Laprovittola, el último gran protagonista
articles.body: Nico Laprovittola tiene 36 años. Ricky Rubio, 35. Y en la final de la Supercopa Endesa, los dos volvieron a demostrar que el DNI no entiende de baloncesto. Pero si hubo un nombre que se salió de la fotografía fue el del argentino, protagonista indiscutible del partido exhibiendo talento, personalidad y capacidad para decidir. Una actuación que sirve como perfecta tarjeta de presentación para una Liga Endesa que, cada vez más, obvia la fecha de nacimiento. Porque hay una Liga que se niega a mirar el DNI. Una Liga en la que la experiencia cotiza al alza, en la que los veteranos siguen teniendo mucho que decir y en la que cumplir 30 años hace tiempo que dejó de ser sinónimo de estar de vuelta o al borde de la jubilación. Los números de la temporada 2026-27 son contundentes: 71 de los 240 jugadores inscritos en la Liga Endesa a día de hoy tienen 30 años o más. Son casi tres de cada diez (29,6%). Y hay otros 20 que han superado los 35. La juventud sigue siendo mayoría —169 jugadores, el 70,4%, tienen menos de 30—, pero la presencia de veteranos ya no es una excepción. Es parte del paisaje. La imagen de Laprovittola y Ricky en la Supercopa no es una anomalía. Es el reflejo de un cambio de época. El veterano ya no está sólo para aportar experiencia, liderazgo o minutos de descanso. Puede ser protagonista, decidir partidos y marcar diferencias. La clave no está en que haya más jugadores mayores como en que los jugadores están consiguiendo ser mayores durante más tiempo. También lo ha hecho la forma de preparar el cuerpo. “El conocimiento que tenemos de todo… alimentación, recuperación… ha hecho que podamos estirar más nuestras carreras”, explicaba Albert Oliver, que se retiró con 43 años. Álex Mumbrú, técnico de la Virtus Bolonia, lo explicaba desde otra perspectiva: “Antes con 35 te tenías que retirar y ahora con la mejora física se alarga la edad de la retirada”. La preparación física, la nutrición, el descanso, la recuperación y la prevención de lesiones se han convertido en esenciales. El jugador dispone de más información y recursos para gestionar su cuerpo. Y hay un segundo factor: el jugador veterano ya no necesita ser el mismo que era a los 23 años. Puede perder explosividad y ganar lectura del juego. Correr menos y pensar antes. Compensar físico con colocación, tiro, dirección, experiencia y decisiones. Huertas, Llull, Tomic, Campazzo, Shermadini, Laprovittola, Ricky Rubio... algunos son estrellas, otros especialistas y otros referentes de vestuario. La Liga Endesa no se arruga. Se reinventa. Y mientras haya piernas para correr, cabeza para interpretar y cuerpos capaces de resistir, la edad será lo de menos. Ya lo dijo Txus Vidorreta, actual entrenador del Unicaja, cuando dirigía a La Laguna Tenerife: “Mientras estén a tope no vamos a mirar el DNI”.

articles.title: 2026 WNBA Awards Picks for MVP, Rookie of the Year, More
articles.summary: The 2026 WNBA regular season is coming to a close this week, so it's time to assess where the major award races stand.
articles.body:
The 2026 WNBA regular season is coming to a close this week, so it's time to assess where the major award races stand.

Some are almost complete locks, while others, particularly Defensive Player of the Year and Most Improved Player, are much more up for debate.

These are our picks for each award, not predictions of what voters will do. But for transparency, we don't have an official ballot. These choices are simply based on how we would vote after evaluating each player's season.

Rotation players from Minnesota's 2025 roster left for contracts over $12 million combined, they missed out on Gabby Williams and Nneka Ogwumike in free agency and Napheesa Collier was sidelined over half of the season due to injury. Yet, they still have the best record in the league.

Cheryl Reeve deserves an enormous amount of credit. It took no time for her to build an elite offense around No. 2 pick Olivia Miles, Natasha Howard is playing like her 2019 self again and Nia Brodie (formerly Coffey) has turned into a quality three-and-D wing again after it looked like her WNBA career might be over following two rough seasons.

Sydney Johnson also deserves major props for getting Washington into the playoffs in just his second season. The same goes for Natalie Nakase, who has Golden State over 30 wins. The Valkyries are one of the few teams in WNBA history to win at least 70 percent of their games without a superstar.

Your pick for Most Improved Player probably comes down to how you define the award. Is it the player who made the biggest statistical jump? Or the player who made the most tangible improvements to their game?

If you believe it's the former, Dallas' Jessica Shepard is the clear pick. She's improved her production across the board, earned an All-Star selection and helped lead the Wings back to the playoffs in the process.

For us, though, Portland guard Carla Leite is the best combination of both. She's increased her scoring by 8.8 points per game while making significant strides as both a shooter and passer. Her three-point percentage jumped by 22.7 percent, while her assist rate increased by 20.3 percent.

Leite is just the 10th player in WNBA history to increase her scoring by at least eight points per game and true shooting percentage by 8 percentage points in a single season, per Across The Timeline .

Washington center Shakira Austin also deserves serious consideration after the star leap she's made this season.

Janelle Salaün has scored 492 points off the bench this season. That's 171 more than her Golden State teammate Tiffany Hayes, who's in second place, and 221 more than the Aces' Jewell Loyd at No. 7, despite playing 104 fewer minutes than Loyd.

Salaün can flat-out score. She can run off screens, spot up and hit step-back jumpers while being almost completely unbothered by closeouts. She's 6'3", and her release is so high that it's impossible to contest.

Salaün is averaging 12.9 points in just 22.3 minutes per game, which translates to 20.9 points per 36 minutes. That's in the same general range as stars like Napheesa Collier and Nneka Ogwumike.

Golden State is 11.9 points per 100 possessions better offensively with Salaün on the court. The Valkyries also have the infrastructure to insulate her defensively, allowing her to just go out there and get buckets.

A week into the season, Olivia Miles was already the runaway Rookie of the Year favorite, and it's only become more clear since then.

Barring a voter throwing a random vote elsewhere, Miles should become the sixth unanimous ROY in WNBA history, joining Aliyah Boston, A'ja Wilson, Elena Delle Donne, Tina Charles and Candace Parker.

At point guard for the Lynx, Miles is the best player on the No. 1 seed, completely taking over games as a pick-and-roll playmaker and driver. And now she's knocking down threes at a high level too, shooting 38.8 percent from deep on a high volume of pull-ups.

Her ability to create shots for herself and others is downright unbelievable. Miles is scoring 19.5 unassisted points per 100 possessions (No. 1 in the league) while posting a true shooting percentage 4.9 points above league average.

She can make virtually every pass, lives at the rim and has the pull-up game to counter defenses when they go under on screens. It's an almost impossible offensive skill set.

Defensive Player of the Year: Shakira Austin

This year's DPOY race is more wide open than ever, with as many as seven players having legitimate cases. You could go in several different directions and have a valid argument, but our pick is Washington Mystics center Shakira Austin.

Austin is anchoring the league's No. 2 defense while leading the youngest playoff team in WNBA history.

She can do just about everything defensively. The 26-year-old is elite at defending in ball screens, with the ability to switch, play at the level or in drop. Her lateral movement and flexibility are special. Austin's active off the ball, rotates quickly and uses her length and athleticism to make plays in help, too.

She's also been remarkably disciplined. Austin is just the 12th player to post a 4 percent block rate and a foul rate below 3 percent in a season (minimum 20 games played and 25 minutes per game), according to HerHoopStats .

Opponents are shooting just 49.7 percent at the rim against Austin this season, the best mark among all WNBA players, according to Yahoo Sports' Nekias Duncan .

Gabby Williams was our original pick, but her minutes load for Golden State is the biggest flaw in her case. She's played more than 300 fewer minutes than Austin this season, and her 24.8 minutes per game would be the lowest average ever for a DPOY winner.

Angel Reese also has a compelling case. Her on/off impact is massive, with the Dream allowing 14 fewer points per 100 possessions with her on the floor (No. 1 in the league). Reese also forces more turnovers than any frontcourt player and consistently ends possessions on the glass.

But as good as Reese has been defensively in space, she doesn't protect the rim anywhere near Austin's level, and Washington's defense has been slightly better overall this season.

Another season, another A'ja Wilson MVP award.

Wilson will likely win her third straight MVP and fifth overall, and she just turned 30 years old last month. At this point, there's a good chance she could pass Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's NBA record six MVPs before her career is over.

Wilson is averaging 26.2 points, 9.3 rebounds and 3.2 assists for the Aces while shooting 54.6 percent from two and 40 percent from three. She's also shooting 86.5 percent from the free-throw line on over eight attempts per game.

Even in what might be a down defensive season by Wilson's standards, she's still one of the five best defenders in the league. She leads the WNBA with 2.0 blocks per game, and her advanced metrics remain off the charts.

Olivia Miles is having a historic season, Breanna Stewart is still a superstar, Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell are offensive monsters. But there really isn't a recency bias argument that could keep Wilson from winning this award.

Nobody has ever impacted the game on both ends quite like her.

articles.title: 'Mandarinas': la historia de Sergio Llull, una leyenda mundial
articles.standfirst: Este miércoles 23 a las 21.00 horas, MARCA.com y la ACB te ofrecen un imprescindible repaso documental a la carrera y la vida del capitán del Real Madrid
articles.summary: Este miércoles 23 a las 21.00 horas, MARCA.com y la ACB te ofrecen un imprescindible repaso documental a la carrera y la vida del capitán del Real Madrid
articles.body: Sergio Llull es una leyenda viva del baloncesto. Viva (no por su estado, claro) porque sigue jugando, sigue en activo. De hecho a sus 38 años (el 15 de noviembre cumplirá 39), se convertirá en el jugador con más temporadas en la Liga Endesa en un mismo club. Este domingo 27 ante el Unicaja comenzará su campaña 21 de blanco, la vigesimosegunda en la Liga Endesa (una con el Manresa). Y es una leyenda por esos datos y porque pocos, muy pocos jugadores en el mundo y en la historia pueden presumir de una carrera como la suya. Ha ganado 30 títulos con el Madrid, más que nadie, incluyendo futbolistas. Y no sólo eso, ha sido capital en la etapa más triunfal de la sección de baloncesto y también de la selección española. Y tiene un número casi incalculable de topes, récords y registros imbatibles. Pero algún día Llull dejará de jugar, como es lógico, y además de dejar tras de sí un legado que será casi imposible de superar, habrá dejado una marca registrada que perdurará para siempre. Tras Llull, cualquier jugador en el mundo que lance un balón sobre la bocina de posesión o de final de cuarto o partido, casi sin posición, con uno o dos defensores encima y desequilibrado y lo anote, habrá logrado una mandarina... como las que Llull ha anotado, como si fuera un tiro sencillo, a lo largo de su carrera. En baloncesto siempre está la pregunta de ¿a quién le darías la última bola jugándote un partido? Desde Llull, sólo hay una respuesta. De todo esto, de cómo asume la responsabilidad de esos tiros, de sus comienzos en Menorca en el colegio La Salle, de su fichaje por el Madrid, de su casi aventura en los Houston Rockets por la insistencia del equipo de la NBA, de su lesión, de su recuperación, de su vuelta, de su vida, de la de una leyenda que trascenderá a su tiempo, trata el documental que la ACB ha dedicado a uno de los jugadores más importantes en el baloncesto mundial en las últimas dos décadas. El nombre del documental que este miércoles se emite en MARCA.com y en el canal de YouTube de la ACB a partir de las 21.00 horas, no puede ser más acertado: 'Mandarinas'. La historia de Sergio Llull. En él hablan sus padres, Paco Llull y Toñi Melià, que recuerdan anécdotas de su infancia y nos muestran la casa familiar y la habitación donde creció Sergio, llena de tesoros. Hablan amigos de toda la vida, compañeros de equipo de cuando anotó 71 puntos para llamar la atención de la FEB, su agente, Ernest Berenguer, que cuenta la intrahistoria de su fichaje por el Madrid y por qué no fue al Barça, o de su 'casi' fichaje por los Rockets de la NBA. También hay palabras de Raül López, compañero suyo en el Madrid y que fue su primer mentor cuando llegó al club, e incluso de Iván Llull, su hermano, que introduce el debate sobre lo que será Sergio cuando se retire. Esta es la historia de Sergio Llull. Un repaso por la vida y la carrera de un jugador único, de una leyenda viva, del creador de las 'Mandarinas'. articles.title: Ranking Los Angeles Lakers' Top Trade Targets for 2026-27 NBA Season
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers have invested heavily in their roster for the coming season, both in contracts (Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Sandro Mamukelashvili) and in draft compensation to acquire Kessler from the Utah Jazz (multiple first-round picks).
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have invested heavily in their roster for the coming season, both in contracts (Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Sandro Mamukelashvili) and in draft compensation to acquire Kessler from the Utah Jazz (multiple first-round picks).

The team needs to be very good this season because it lacks the means to improve significantly via trade. Outside of one full first-round pick swap in 2032 and three future seconds, the Lakers are spent. Would Trey Murphy III fit exceptionally well on the squad? Of course, but L.A. has nothing of real value to offer the New Orleans Pelicans outside of its top players like Luka Dončić, Reaves, and Kessler.

Still, the Lakers may seek a minor trade before the season starts to get down to the required 15 standard contracts from their current 16. While they still need starting-caliber forwards, that's just on paper. The front office may wait until trade season, from mid-December to the February trade deadline, to get a real look at how the pieces fit together—but some potential targets are easy to identify.

After moving on from LeBron James, Marcus Smart, and other veterans, the Lakers have tried to get younger.

Indiana Pacers forward Jarace Walker, 23, is in the final year of his rookie-scale contract as the No. 8 overall pick in 2023.

At 6'7", Walker is more of a perimeter scorer than a bruising power forward, but he's athletic and would add additional depth to the Lakers' frontcourt. The Pacers have consistently avoided the luxury tax, so it's surprising the franchise projects to be over this year by as much as $6.4 million. Many competing executives expect the team to trim somewhere ahead of the trade deadline to get under the $200.4 million threshold.

Walker is the most obvious, expendable player at $8.5 million. The Lakers would need to send out, though they may need a third team to take on one of Dalton Knecht, Jaden Hardy, or Jake LaRavia, to help the Pacers avoid the tax.

A more complicated deal can be constructed around Obi Toppin and Walker, including Jarred Vanderbilt, but as of the last check, the Pacers still prioritize Toppin in the rotation.

No. 4: De'Andre Hunter, Sacramento Kings

The Sacramento Kings acquired De'Andre Hunter from the Cleveland Cavaliers ahead of the last deadline, getting a solid forward at a relatively low price, as the Kings were ready to move on from guards Keon Ellis and Dennis Schröder.

On paper, the franchise doesn't look highly competitive in the Western Conference this season. The team drafted Darius Acuff Jr. with the No. 7 pick, but he'll need time to develop. Hunter is in the final year of his deal, and unless Sacramento intends to extend him, the team should get the best available return before the February deadline.

Hunter, 29 in December, has shot the three-ball well over most of his career, but he dropped from 40.5 percent in 2024-25 to 30.5 percent last season. The Lakers would want to see that he's healthy—durability has been an issue throughout Hunter's career—and shooting well before making an offer.

At $24.9 million, Hunter also has an unlikely $1.3 million incentive that counts against the first apron. The Lakers may need to include Vanderbilt and the 2032 first-round pick swap, or at least multiple second-rounders to give the Kings enough motivation for a deal.

While he's 6'7" and can play either forward spot, Hunter isn't necessarily burly enough to man that position against some of the stronger power forwards.

The LA Clippers have shifted direction after a difficult year, trading Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors. The completed investigation stripped the team of five first-round picks, but they recouped others from Toronto in the Leonard swap.

Initially, the Clippers will see what the veterans can do together with Brandon Ingram, Darius Garland, Max Strus, former Lakers forward Rui Hachimura, and Derrick Jones Jr., among others. The real priority is building for the future by developing Keaton Wagler and other young players while preserving long-term flexibility.

LA may struggle to rebuild via the draft and through trade without movable first-round picks; cap room appears to be the path forward. That could make the Clippers a seller by the deadline.

Jones is in the final year of his deal at $10.5 million. He was a productive teammate of Dončić in Dallas during the Mavericks' NBA Finals run. He's athletic, defends, and has a strong enough three-ball to keep teams honest.

The Lakers could build a trade around players like Knecht, LaRavia, and Hardy, but the Clippers would prioritize draft considerations. The Lakers only have the first-round swap in 2032 available (outside of swapping already-swapped firsts, which don't hold as much appeal), but the Clippers don't have a 2032 first to work with.

Jones seems more like a deadline option, with the Clippers not getting any offers greater than the three second-round picks the Lakers can send. While he'd fill an important role as a wing stopper, Jones wouldn't solve the Lakers' frontcourt depth issues.

Ranking 5 NBA Teams With the Worst Salary-Cap Situations 😖

The Mavericks have changed significantly since trading Dončić to the Lakers, with shifts across the front office and coaching staff. PJ Washington was extended last year, but Dallas has increasingly loaded up at his position with Santiago Aldama, Zaccharie Risacher, and last year's No. 1 overall pick, Cooper Flagg.

The latest word from various NBA sources is that Washington's trade market is barren. The four-year, $88.8 million obligation is too rich for any real suitors ahead of the season, including the Lakers.

However, as the season progresses, if L.A. recognizes its need at power forward, Washington is a strong fit as a former Dončić teammate who is a willing role player, defender, and shooter. He's not as accurate from three-point range as the Lakers would want, but Washington knows well where Dončić is going to get him the ball and is willing to let it fly.

The Lakers' advantage in going after Washington is that Dallas would probably be happy to take Vanderbilt's $13.3 million player option for 2027-28 to get out of Washington's longer deal.

Washington would help the Lakers on the court, but it's more a question of the team's appetite for the long-term financial obligation.

The Lakers drafted Randle No. 7 overall in 2014. According to his own account, Randle set massively illegal screens for Kobe Bryant in the 60-point final and legendary game of his career. Now nearing 32, Randle is a three-time All-Star and the kind of physical presence the Lakers don't have on the roster.

Respectfully, Randle is a bully on the court. He can score (21.1 points per game last season for the Minnesota Timberwolves) and pass (5.0 assists), but what impressed the Lakers most when they drafted him was his brute strength. He's not a perfect defender, but he fit in well on a strong Minnesota defensive unit. Randle has shot well from three before, but his career 33.2 percent isn't ideal.

Still, if he's available, Randle would give the Lakers a very different frontcourt alongside Kessler, with Mamukelashvili backing him up. The Timberwolves sent him to the Brooklyn Nets this summer in the LaMelo Ball blockbuster. Randle doesn't fit the Nets' timeline, and while they probably won't deal him before the season starts, he's definitely a player to watch ahead of the trade deadline.

Randle is expensive at $33.3 million. The Lakers would need to include LaRavia, Hardy, Knecht, and Vanderbilt, which would be problematic for the Nets in-season with the 15-man roster limit. A multi-team deal, which has become more common in the NBA, would help.

Randle has a $35.8 million player option for 2027-28. If the Lakers are willing to pay him a new three-year contract—timed with a player option with Reaves, Kessler, Grimes, and Mamukelashvili before 2029-30—and Randle is willing to take a lower starting figure in the $25 million range, L.A. would still have its non-taxpayer mid-level exception at about $16 million next summer.

Instead of Randle, the Lakers could try to acquire his current teammate, Michael Porter Jr., from the Nets; however, a lack of assets and his $40.8 million salary this season make it prohibitive under L.A.'s first-apron hard cap. The math could work later in the year, but the Lakers would need to add Grimes or Mamukelashvili—in addition to Vanderbilt, LaRavia, Hardy and Knecht.

Getting large deals like that done during the regular season is complicated, as teams cannot take on more than 15 players under standard contracts. Porter isn't a "no," but a first-round pick swap and three seconds feels awfully light to Brooklyn.

The Lakers may be better off finding a team looking to get out of salary, like the Orlando Magic, who are surprisingly above the luxury tax threshold despite consistently avoiding penalties. Goga Bitadze would be a strong backup to Walker Kessler, though the Magic seem fond of the Georgian center.

The Denver Nuggets are the only team in the league above the second apron. Would they be willing to send Cam Johnson to Los Angeles? The Lakers would also need a third team to help the Magic or Nuggets reduce salary.

The Lakers would be reluctant to take on Jerami Grant's $36.4 million option for 2027-28 from the Memphis Grizzlies. While Isaiah Stewart II would appeal, he'd be more expensive for L.A. to acquire. Similarly, the Pelicans want too much for Herb Jones.

articles.title: Breanna Stewart blames technical foul on Angel Reese, demands Dream star 'pay my fine'
articles.summary: Breanna Stewart last received a technical foul in 2017.
articles.body:
Breanna Stewart and Angel Reese appeared to work well together during their gold-medal win at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup. But any of that support was apparently lost the instant the two went back to their WNBA teams.

Reese and Stewart found themselves at the center of a contentious moment during Monday's game between the Atlanta Dream and New York Liberty , one that Stewart decided to escalate after the contest.

The issue stemmed from a missing foul call on Reese with just under two minutes to play. With the Liberty down by eight, Stewart stopped a drive to the lane to try for a pull-up jumper. Reese knocked the ball away, stealing it to give the Dream possession.

Since it was so late in the contest, Reese was immediately fouled, and Stewart decided to tear into the refs, claiming she was fouled by Reese.

But Stewart took her criticism way too far, and was hit with a technical foul.

Upon looking at the replay, Stewart appeared to have a point.

Stewart didn't get her way during the game. Reese hit both free throws and the Dream went on to win the contest 95-84 .

But time apparently didn't heal all wounds in this case. Stewart was still hot after the game, telling reporters Reese "slapped [the] s*** out of my hand" on the play. As Stewart left the end-of-game presser, she yelled out, "Angel should pay my fine."

This is mostly uncharted territory for Stewart, who — prior to Monday — last received a technical foul back in 2017, her second year in the league , per ESPN. Reese is already far more accomplished in that area, and is — like Caitlin Clark — sitting on seven technical fouls this season.

Given that, Reese probably shouldn't be expected to spend more money paying for technical fouls, especially ones that weren't called on her.

As for Stewart, she could have a chance to get revenge in the playoffs. Should the two teams meet in the postseason, Stewart could send Reese home early, which would more than make up for Stewart paying her own technical-foul fine.

articles.title: Must-watch Wizards? Trae Young, Anthony Davis, AJ Dybantsa and the NBA's weirdest group project
articles.summary: Washington's two-timeline experiment makes it one of the most unpredictable teams in the league this season.
articles.body:
The Wizards spent the past few years trying to lose. Now they're trying to win and develop players at the same time. Half the roster is young, the other half is old. But all of them are trying to figure out who they are. Washington is running a two-timeline experiment that features veterans Trae Young , Anthony Davis , Khris Middleton and Deandre Ayton . That group could accelerate or get in the way of the development of Washington's interesting young core. This is the NBA's weirdest group project.

The Wizards have a bunch of prospects who were drafted over the three seasons in which the franchise combined for only 50 wins: AJ Dybantsa, Tre Johnson , Alex Sarr , Kyshawn George , Will Riley and Bub Carrington . There's a lot of talent here. There are also a lot of mouths to feed. And nobody matters more to making it work than Young, who was acquired in January from the Atlanta Hawks , played in only five games to aid Washington's tank, and then was rewarded with a four-year, $212 million extension.

Young has spent his entire career as the center of an offense, pounding the ball in pick-and-roll and creating shots for everyone on the floor. As a four-time All-Star, what he's done has led to great individual success, and he even led Atlanta to the Eastern Conference finals in 2021. But that run proved to be the peak. The Hawks never won another playoff series with Young, cycled through coaches and supporting casts, and ultimately decided to pull the plug.

Washington can't afford for this to become The Trae Young Show. Even if the Young-Davis pick-and-roll becomes one of Washington's most reliable weapons, the offense still needs to leave room for all of the young players to experiment, make mistakes and expand their games. The Wizards need to learn what they can become, which makes Young's willingness to evolve the biggest question hanging over this roster.

Can Trae learn to play without the ball?

Sometimes the greatest contribution a player can make is the gravity he creates by sprinting hard through a screen, relocating to the corner after making a pass, or simply standing 28 feet from the rim. Young entered the 2018 draft drawing comparisons to Steph Curry and Damian Lillard because of this skill, but too often nowadays he plays like his job is done once he gives up the ball.

It wasn't like that in college at Oklahoma. Young looks like a totally different player in some of these clips from his freshman year with the Sooners:

He ran through screens. He relocated off the ball. He got himself open. This was part of the appeal that Atlanta saw in trading up for him. Because even though he was primarily a high-usage shot-creator in college, he also willingly played off the ball and shined whenever he did. But it's become a rare sight in the NBA.

Since Trae entered the NBA, he's shot out of an off-ball screening action just 0.4 times per game. That's nine times less often than Steph and more than twice less often than Dame during this same timeframe, as the below chart shows.

Steph is obviously an outlier-level, all-time great shooter — and that comparison was never really fair to Trae — but Trae posts a scoring efficiency about equal to Dame in this action. Instead of absorbing even Dame-level off-ball usage, though, Young has leaned into his inner James Harden as an initiator who remains stationary off-ball. One of the skills that made him such an appealing draft prospect is lost.

But when Young does receive the ball off the catch? He produces! He has made 39.4% of his catch-and-shoot 3s in his career, a strong number that ranks in the 70th percentile of the 233 shooters to log at least 700 shots over that span. The issue is he's taken only 725 of those shots in his 498-game career, a mere 1.5 per game. It's a tiny amount compared to 3s off the bounce:

By no means should Young become some type of specialist given his creative talents as a passer and playmaker. But he should not be taking four times as many 3s off the dribble as he does 3s off the catch when his efficiency is so much better in spot-up situations.

Atlanta's rosters never really had the amount of young talent worth investing in that Washington does. And Young has never been more doubted than he is at this moment. So if there's any time to sacrifice and prove everyone wrong, it's now.

Can the vets help without getting in the way?

The player worth the biggest investment was just drafted with the first pick: Dybantsa, who already has the 6-foot-9 size and natural scoring instincts to have a high floor as a rookie after leading the nation with 25.5 points per game as a freshman. He bends around defenders and explodes to the rim with the body control to draw fouls and the touch to cook in the midrange. His flashes as a passer hint that he has point forward potential too.

All of which makes Dybantsa's fit with Young one of the most fascinating dynamics on the roster. The Wizards can't spend Dybantsa's rookie season treating him like a role player just because a veteran point guard is better at running an offense today. If Young finds the right balance, it will help set the Wizards on a path toward playing winning basketball.

The same principle applies to the other young guys. Middleton should be an easy fit. At age 35, he doesn't need to play 30 minutes or take 20 shots. But if head coach Brian Keefe starts feeding important minutes to Middleton instead of Johnson, Wizards fans are gonna be protesting. Johnson was the sixth pick one year ago and just had one of the best midrange-shooting seasons in the NBA. Middleton should be mentoring him on how to extend his range to 3 and how to find angles to get to the rim, not stealing his minutes.

George arguably has even greater potential than Johnson. Drafted 24th in 2024, George is 6-8 and had seven games with at least 20 points, five assists and five boards before his year ended in March. He's the type of player who can impact the game across the box score in different ways on different nights. The Wizards need to find out how those skills translate to a winning atmosphere, so his minutes should trend up, not down.

On paper, Davis should be an additive piece in the frontcourt next to Sarr. With his size and experience, maybe the Wizards might actually start getting stops. The last time the Wizards had a top-10 defensive rating was 2014-15. It's been over a decade! But the word is that AD and the Wizards plan to spend some time together before deciding on his potential contract extension. Will he play all 82 games as he predicted? Or is he still made of glass? Do contenders try to scoop him from the Wizards? Could the Wizards pay him the full max and cause Wizards fans to have a heart attack?

The worst version is easy to imagine. AD gets hurt or the extension situation becomes a distraction, Trae inhales touches, and the young guys get squeezed. The best version is Young shares control of the offense, Davis anchors the defense, and the kids all get freedom to experiment. The Wizards could suddenly become competitive without sacrificing the future.

Trying to simultaneously win and develop is what makes Washington one of the NBA's most unpredictable teams. And for the first time in years, that makes the Wizards must-watch basketball.

articles.title: Willy Hernangómez se adueña de la pintura del Unicaja
articles.standfirst: El pívot español ha sido el mejor de la pretemporada cajista
articles.summary: El pívot español ha sido el mejor de la pretemporada cajista
articles.body: El Unicaja ya tiene la pretemporada prácticamente en el retrovisor y el inicio de la Liga Endesa aparece en el horizonte. Han sido semanas con varios condicionantes para Txus Vidorreta: el pívot que falta por llegar, las lesiones de Tyler Kalinoski y Yannick Nzosa, las molestias de Tyson Pérez... Pero también ha habido una noticia especialmente positiva. Willy Hernangómez ha sido el mejor del equipo durante la preparación. No era difícil imaginar que el madrileño iba a ser uno de los grandes focos de atención de la nueva temporada. Su pasado en la NBA y sus tres años en el Barcelona le colocaban directamente bajo los focos desde el primer día. Lo que quizá no estaba tan claro era que fuese a asumir tan pronto ese papel protagonista. Los números hablan por sí solos. Willy ha disputado cinco amistosos y se marcha de la pretemporada con 12,8 puntos, 6,4 rebotes y 17,2 de valoración por partido. No estuvo en Melilla porque estaba con la selección, pero sí dejó dos actuaciones especialmente llamativas. Contra La Laguna Tenerife firmó un doble-doble de 16 puntos y 11 rebotes y ante el Monbus Obradoiro se fue hasta los 21 puntos y 10 rebotes. Y hay algo más allá de las estadísticas. En varios momentos ha sido el jugador al que el Unicaja ha buscado cuando el partido pedía una solución cerca del aro. Ahí está buena parte de su valor. Porque sí, las dudas sobre su defensa siguen existiendo y sería absurdo esconderlas. Pero también se habla demasiado poco de todo lo que puede hacer en ataque. Willy tiene recursos de sobra para jugar de espaldas, encontrar diferentes maneras de finalizar y castigar a los interiores rivales. Y eso, en un equipo que todavía está terminando de construirse, puede tener mucho peso. Además, el contexto puede hacer que su responsabilidad sea todavía mayor. Nzosa está lesionado, Kravish continúa recuperando sensaciones después de su fractura de peroné y Juanma Rodríguez sigue buscando en el mercado ese pívot que termine de completar la rotación. Por ahora, Vidorreta tiene una certeza. Willy ha llegado para jugar y la pretemporada le ha colocado ya en primera línea. Ahora toca comprobar si ese protagonismo se mantiene cuando empiece lo serio.

articles.title: Tyrese Haliburton's New Pacers-Inspired Colorway of 'Hali 1' Revealed in Photo Ahead of Return
articles.summary: Tyrese Haliburton will return to the court during the 2026-27 NBA season, and he will be doing so in style.
articles.body:
Tyrese Haliburton will return to the court during the 2026-27 NBA season, and he will be doing so in style.

Puma announced Tuesday it is releasing a new colorway inspired by the Indiana Pacers for the guard's signature Hali 1 PACE shoe.

"The Hali 1 PACE embodies a mindset of unwavering self-belief," the press release explained. "It doesn't ignore criticism, it embraces it and turns it into motivation. Serving as a bold response to the doubters and a statement of what's ahead, the Hali 1 PACE marks Tyrese Haliburton's return to the game with 0 DOUBT."

Ranking 5 NBA Teams With the Worst Salary-Cap Situations 😖

The shoe, which was designed by Salehe Bembury, will be available Oct. 23 from Puma's website and app, as well as at Champs and Foot Locker, for $130.

It features nitrogen-infused cushioning, non-slip rubber compound for traction and a midfoot shank for more stability and support.

The timing is notable, as Oct. 23 is the Pacers' home opener against the Dallas Mavericks this season.

It will mark the first time Haliburton is back on the floor for a regular-season game in Indiana since the 2024-25 campaign. He suffered a torn Achilles during Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals and missed the entire 2025-26 season as he recovered.

Beloved by Pacers fans, Haliburton led the team to the NBA Finals with a combination of incredible buzzer beaters and comebacks during the 2025 playoffs. They pushed Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the Oklahoma City Thunder to a decisive seventh game but ultimately fell short after he suffered the injury.

His return figures to make Indiana one of the top contenders in the Eastern Conference once again during the upcoming season, and he will have a new colorway for his signature shoe inspired by the team he represents.

articles.title: Willy y su recibimiento en Madrid: "Soy madridista, será diferente"
articles.standfirst: El pívot vuelve a la que fue su casa este domingo para enfrentarse al Madrid con el Unicaja
articles.summary: El pívot vuelve a la que fue su casa este domingo para enfrentarse al Madrid con el Unicaja
articles.body: El Unicaja inicia el próximo domingo 27 su temporada oficial, pero en realidad inicia una nueva era, con muchos cambios con respecto a la temporada pasada y un nuevo líder en la pintura: Willy Hernangómez. El pívot fue uno de los protagonistas del Media day del equipo malagueño a pocos días de su debut en la Liga Endesa que será precisamente en el Movistar Arena ante el Real Madrid. Willy habló de varios aspectos de su proceso de adaptación a un nuevo equipo y a otro entrenador, Txus Vidorreta. Pero dejó una perla cuando le preguntaron por el recibimiento que esperaba en Madrid, ¿pitos o aplausos? “No me tienen ganas. Siempre estaré agradecido al Real Madrid y a los aficionados. Es el club donde crecí. Soy madridista. Siempre estaré apoyándolos y animándolos. Ahora llego con otra perspectiva porque lo hago con el Unicaja y no con el Barça y creo que será diferente”. Así de sincero se mostraba un Willy pitado siempre en sus visitas con el Barça a Madrid en las tres temporadas que jugó de azulgrana. El jugador estima que esta vez será diferente. Willy aprovechó para hablar del aspecto deportivo del estreno de su nuevo equipo ante el Madrid: "El partido del domingo es muy duro y está siendo muy bien entrenado por Pedro Martínez. Están jugando increíble y han ganado la Supercopa de la Euroliga. Y también vimos su nivel en el Carpena. Pero ahora empieza la Liga y lo serio". El pívot, que ya ha demostrado en la pretemporada lo mucho que puede aportar al Unicaja, analizó su relación con su nuevo entrenador: "He encajado muy bien con Txus. En su filosofía, en la forma que quiere que juguemos, que tenga peso en la pista en ambas mitades de la pista y que tenga responsabilidad y tome decisiones". Y sobre el Unicaja y el Willy que pueden ver en el Carpena: "Ojalá veamos al Willy del Eurobasket de Alemania. Estoy recuperando muchas sensaciones y me siento feliz en la pista. Me noto más dominante en la pista y disfruto mucho con los compañeros".

articles.title: Trae Young Reveals He Didn't Feel 'As Comfortable' with Hawks After Onsi Saleh Was Hired as GM
articles.summary: Four-time NBA All-Star Trae Young sensed an internal shift within the Atlanta Hawks once Onsi Saleh took over as the leading voice inside the front office.
articles.body:
Four-time NBA All-Star Trae Young sensed an internal shift within the Atlanta Hawks once Onsi Saleh took over as the leading voice inside the front office.

"I love the owner, Tony (Ressler), and all the ownership group and everybody down there," Young said on Michael Porter Jr.'s Curious Mike podcast (via Josh Robbins of The Athletic). "So I have much love to a lot of people down there in Atlanta, so I never wanted to leave (in) a bad way. But once we got on that third GM, and we brought in Onsi, it's like you don't necessarily feel as comfortable as you did (when) you got there. … There are so many things I won't say until later on, but sometimes it's just better just to let things go."

Ranking 5 NBA Teams With the Worst Salary-Cap Situations 😖

A new general manager or president of basketball operations can always be a little disruptive for a player who's positioned as the franchise cornerstone.

In the case of Young, Saleh wasn't the GM who acquired him in a draft-night trade in 2018 or gave him a max extension in 2021.

Saleh was first brought to Atlanta as assistant general manager in 2024 and got promoted to the top job a year later. This past May, he earned another promotion to president of basketball ops.

Young told Porter he knew Saleh's ascension was potentially a big change to the status quo.

"I've experienced, obviously, the one that drafted me, and then we brought in another GM who made some (changes)," he said. "And so when we brought our third one … we all knew around me that it's either we're going to be around here for the long haul and we win or it may be time for everybody to just part their ways."

Along with that, the Hawks' performance raised questions over whether building around Young remained the best path forward. Following a trip to the 2021 Eastern Conference Finals, Atlanta suffered two straight first-round exits and didn't make the postseason at all in 2023 or 2024.

Young's trade to the Washington Wizards illustrated how far his stock had fallen. It was effectively a salary dump as the Hawks didn't get a single draft pick back.

His exit from Atlanta was probably inevitable from the moment Travis Schlenk stepped down in December 2022. Young lost his biggest advocate in the organization.

It sounds like Saleh took a more dispassionate approach toward the 6'2" guard and what needed to happen to move the Hawks forward.

articles.title: Shaq — yes, the NBA legend — is headlining an NFL halftime show
articles.summary: O'Neal has never been one to ignore the spotlight during his glittering career. He has no plans on doing so when he takes to Caesars Superdome on Sunday afte...
articles.body:
Known for his flair and candor, Shaquille O'Neal has never been one to ignore the spotlight.

If anything, the Basketball Hall of Famer bathes in the glow. He was a memorable presence on the floor. In retirement, he has proven similarly noteworthy, cementing his status as one of sport's grandest personalities on "Inside the NBA."

A pop culture icon, O'Neal will return to center stage on Sunday afternoon when the Saints take on the Raiders . It's just not in the way one might initially expect.

With that, here's what you need to know about O'Neal's impending performance at New Orleans' Week 2 halftime show (yes, seriously).

Why Shaq is headlining an NFL halftime show

O'Neal will take to New Orleans — a stone's throw from his old stomping grounds in Baton Rouge — to soundtrack the Saints' clash with the Raiders.

While O'Neal has flaunted his musicality before — he released four rap albums during the 1990s, including "Shaq Diesel," which went platinum — he has transitioned to a new form of music. The Basketball Hall of Famer goes by DJ Diesel now, spurning his rap persona for electronic music.

O'Neal released his first album under the Diesel moniker in 2023. His songs teem with his musical influences; the 2023 tape, "Gorilla Warfare", featured hints of dubstep, house, trap and hip-hop. He'll still occasionally bring the bars — O'Neal dropped a verse on Redman's "Lite It Up" in 2024.

But at this point in his career, O'Neal is most fluent with his turntables. He'll be tasked with setting the mood as New Orleans attempts to push itself above .500 with a win over its much-maligned adversary.

O'Neal was born in New Jersey. He played high school ball in Texas, having moved there when his father, a member of the U.S. military, was transferred to a base in San Antonio. O'Neal also spent time in Georgia and Germany during his youth. Despite this, he still regards New Jersey — and more specifically, Newark — as his home.

"Newark is really still home, where my relatives live," O'Neal wrote in his autobiography . "I can always go back and see the people I grew up with."

Despite his Newark roots, the state of Louisiana was quite consequential to his on-court success.

O'Neal attended LSU, shining on Dale Brown's team alongside Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf (born Chris Jackson). A two-time All-American, two-time SEC Player of the Year recipient and the 1991 Adolph Rupp Trophy winner, O'Neal was inducted into the LSU Hall of Fame.

A 900-pound statue of him was erected in front of the Tigers' practice facility in 2011.

articles.title: Will Victor Wembanayama and the Spurs play in front of sold-out arenas in Europe?
articles.summary: The NBA gave an update on Tuesday on the reception the defending Western Conference champions are expected to receive in Paris and Manchester in January.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama and Co. are a hot ticket on two continents.

The Spurs will play their two games in Europe this season in front of sold-out crowds, reflecting the popularity of the Wembanyama-led defending Western Conference champions, the NBA announced Tuesday.

Per the league, approximately one million fans registered their interest in tickets, marking the highest level of demand ever recorded for NBA games in Europe.

The Spurs, who are expected to again compete for the NBA title this season after losing in five games to New York in the Finals last season, are set to face the New Orleans Pelicans in regular season games on Jan. 14 at Accor Arena in Paris and on Jan. 17 at Co-op Live in Manchester, England, as part of the league's multi-year slate of regular season games in Europe.

Both events will stream live on Amazon Prime Video.

The Spurs are no strangers to Europe, having played two games in Paris in January 2025 against the Indiana Pacers in a much-anticipated series that marked Wembanyama's first action as an NBA player in his home country.

"I'm sure it'll be a great trip," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said in May after the NBA announced the Spurs would be returning to Europe. "(We're) always looking forward to expanding the game and being part of the cool process of being able to play outside the country."

With French fans cheering his every step during the 2025 trip, Wembanyama hosted a dinner and a shopping spree for the Spurs in the City of Light before guiding the team through his hometown of Le Chasnay on the outskirts of Paris.

The trip left lasting memories, several players said.

"Oh, man, I love Paris," forward Julian Champagnie said. "It was a great experience. The people are great. The fans are great. The place is great. Obviously, I've never been to Manchester. I'm excited to go, though. It's going to be fun. I think we're up for it."

articles.title: Hawks news: Trae Young throws shade at GM after revealing how KD, Russ' Thunder exits inspired Atlanta departure
articles.summary: Washington Wizards guard Trae Young reflected on his Atlanta Hawks days, talking about president of basketball operations Onsi Saleh and how leaving on good...
articles.body:
Washington Wizards guard Trae Young reflected on his Atlanta Hawks days, talking about president of basketball operations Onsi Saleh and how leaving on good terms mattered to Trae. After watching what happened with Kevin Durant , Russell Westbrook , and the Oklahoma City Thunder , Young hoped to maintain a relationship similar to Westbrook's, who's revered by Thunder fans in OKC.

After the Hawks traded Young to the Wizards in a blockbuster move last season, he believes it was the right thing for both sides. Plus, Young isn't ruling out a potential reunion with the Hawks at some point in the future, he said, per the Curious Mike podcast.

"I knew it was time, and for me, I wanted to leave the right way. I never wanted it to be a big deal. I grew up in OKC, where I saw KD get killed for leaving a certain way; I didn't want that type of feeling. I also saw how they treated Russ when he ended up leaving OKC. So I wanted to figure out how I wanted to leave, and you never know how the NBA works. So, you never know if a rekindle is in the future."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Trae Young received a heartfelt Hawks video tribute in his first game as a Wizard in Atlanta. When All-Star Kevin Durant signed with the Golden State Warriors after he and the Thunder blew a 3-1 lead in the 2016 Western Conference Finals, fans vilified him, whereas Russell Westbrook stuck around.

Young also addressed the Hawks front office, including the president of basketball operations, Onsi Saleh.

"I loved the owners, Tony, and all the ownership they got down there. So, I have much love for the people down in Atlanta," Young said. "So, I never wanted to leave in a bad way. Once you got to that in that third GM, and we brought on Onsi, you don't necessarily feel as comfortable as you did when you first got there. It wasn't no big deal to me, neither, and there's so many things I won't say until later on. But sometimes it's better to just let things go."

Young signed a four-year, $212 million contract extension with the Wizards over the summer.

articles.body:
Kyrie Irving released a new collection of his signature ANTA KAI collection ahead of his return for the Dallas Mavericks.

A "Protect Your Sisters" capsule designed in collaboration with Irving's sisters Asia and London was released Saturday on ANTA's website and at the brand's store in Beverly Hills, according to the ANTA Instagram .

The capsule includes the ANTA Hélà Style "Roots" sneaker, a pink, purple and yellow shoe retailing for $130.

The sole of the shoe features Irving's No. 11 and an etching of "Hélà Chief," which ANTA describes as a nod to Irving's Indigenous heritage.

Irving announced his signature deal with ANTA in 2023. The ANTA KAI 1 debuted the following year.

Irving sat out the entire 2025-26 season after tearing his left ACL in March 2025. He could play alongside Cooper Flagg for the first time in regular-season action when the Mavericks tip off the campaign Oct. 21 at the Houston Rockets.

articles.title: NBA Says Paris, Manchester Games Featuring Wemby & Zion Drove Record Ticket Demand
articles.summary: NBA fans in Europe are eager to see Victor Wembanyama play in person.
articles.body:
NBA fans in Europe are eager to see Victor Wembanyama play in person.

The NBA announced Tuesday that the games between Wembanyama's San Antonio Spurs and Zion Williamson' New Orleans Pelicans set to take place in Europe during the upcoming season sold out after approximately a million fans registered interest in tickets.

San Antonio and New Orleans will face each other at Accor Arena in Paris, France, on Thursday, Jan. 14, before playing again at Co-op Live in Manchester, England, on Sunday, Jan. 17. The games will air on Amazon Prime Video.

Wembanyama being involved surely played a role in the historic interest.

The French superstar is coming off a season where he helped lead the Spurs to the NBA Finals. While they fell short against the New York Knicks, it felt like the first of many times fans will get to see him competing on such a stage.

The 22-year-old already has a resume that features a Rookie of the Year, Western Conference Finals MVP, Defensive Player of the Year, three block titles and an All-NBA First Team selection.

Wembanyama finished third in MVP voting last season while averaging 25.0 points, 11.5 rebounds, 3.1 blocks, 3.1 assists and 1.0 steals per game.

And now fans in Europe will get to see him perform in his home continent while facing another notable player in Williamson.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard, Raptors Agree to New Contract After Clippers Trade, Details Revealed
articles.summary: After returning to the Toronto Raptors in a trade from the Los Angeles Clippers, Kawhi Leonard has inked a new deal.
articles.body:
After returning to the Toronto Raptors in a trade from the Los Angeles Clippers, Kawhi Leonard has inked a new deal.

The star signed a two-year, $115 million contract with the Raptors, with a player option for the 2028-29 season, agent Harrison Gaines told ESPN's Shams Charania on Tuesday.

Leonard was previously on a three-year, $149.5 million deal through the 2026-27 season that he signed with the Clippers in 2024.

The Clippers first agreed to trade Leonard to the Raptors on June 30 for a package that included Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and picks, but the deal wasn't finalized until Sept. 14 as the NBA continued its investigation into Los Angeles over salary cap circumvention.

The trade reunited Leonard and the Raptors after seven years apart.

Leonard's first tenure in Toronto was brief but memorable. He had one of the best regular seasons of his career before leading the Raptors to their first and only championship.

Leonard put together one of the best individual playoff runs of all time, averaging 30.5 points, 9.1 rebounds and 1.7 steals per game on the way to winning Finals MVP.

The Leonard who returned to the Raptors this offseason is much older and has dealt with various injuries over the past few years, so he might not be the same version that brought a title to Toronto.

Still, Leonard had an outstanding 2025-26 campaign that saw him put up 27.9 points, 6.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.9 steals per game in 65 contests with the Clippers.

He might not be at the peak of his prime anymore, but he's still one of the best players in the league when he's healthy.

The Raptors have their work cut out for them competing in a stacked Eastern Conference, but the pairing of Leonard and Scottie Barnes should keep them in the mix.

And now having signed a new deal with Toronto, Leonard is committed to the Raptors for at least a few more seasons.

articles.title: Raptors' Kawhi Leonard gets $115M contract update following controversial exit from Clippers
articles.summary: The Toronto Raptors went out this summer and got a familiar face. The Raptors just locked him up for even longer on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Toronto Raptors are looking to be competitive in the Eastern Conference this season. They made an aggressive move to acquire Kawhi Leonard from the Los Angeles Clippers in a trade.

"The trade sending Kawhi Leonard from the LA Clippers to Toronto has been made official after a monthslong delay due to the NBA's investigation into the Clippers for salary cap circumvention. The teams initially agreed to the deal on June 30, but it was paused while the league investigated allegations the Clippers violated salary cap rules in signing Leonard as a free agent," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote.

It is clear that Leonard wanted to return to Toronto, which is where he won his second NBA championship. The two-time NBA champion could have received a contract extension worth $126 million.

"The Toronto Raptors and Kawhi Leonard have held advanced discussions and are nearing an agreement on a contract extension, according to league sources. Leonard is eligible to sign for upwards of two years, $126 million," Bleacher Report's Jake Fischer posted.

The Raptors organization values Leonard at a high level, and he clearly values the organization as well. On Tuesday, the two sides were able to work out a contract extension worth $115 million.

"Toronto Raptors All-NBA star Kawhi Leonard has agreed on a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the franchise, plus a player option for the 2028-29 season, his agent Harrison Gaines of SLASH Sports tells ESPN," Charania posted.

This is huge news for Toronto, as the Raptors now have a future with Leonard and can build around him on a win-now timeline. The Raptors are going to be a playoff-contending team this season, and perhaps one more move could get them into title contention.

Leonard got his money while staying where it feels like home to him and his family. The Raptors are going to take care of Leonard for as long as he wants to be there, which seems to be the rest of his career.

articles.title: Two Duke alums selected in mock NBA expansion draft
articles.summary: A couple of former Blue Devils were recently selected in an NBA expansion mock draft.
articles.body:
With NBA expansion on the table, basketball fans may see two new franchises compete at the highest level very soon. But, considering the last expansion draft took place in 2004, what might the rosters look like? And, of course, would they include any notable Duke alumni?

Bleacher Report gave a partial answer to that question, as two of their writers conducted an NBA expansion mock draft , selecting players from a select group (excluding players expected to be protected in the draft) to round out their rosters. Bleacher Report's staff didn't waste any time selecting a former Blue Devil, taking Jared McCain ( Oklahoma City Thunder ) with the No. 1 overall pick.

While McCain may not be the best player available, his age, production and salary (still on his rookie deal) make him one of the more valuable players on the board. Last season between the Thunder and 76ers , McCain averaged 8.3 points, two rebounds, 1.3 assists and 0.5 steals. He also performed quite well for Oklahoma City in the postseason.

The next and final former Blue Devil selected (No. 11) was Charlotte Hornets guard Sion James . Despite being selected in the second round of last year's 2025 NBA Draft, James carved out a role in Charlotte's rotation, playing in all 82 games. He averaged 5.4 points, 3.5 rebounds, two assists and 0.6 steals. Like McCain, the fact that James is still on his rookie deal makes him a worthy selection.
